messages.text: Heads up, the LCR number on the ReportingBI liquidity dashboard shows 128% this morning vs 134% in yesterday's close pack. Anyone know if there was a methodology change or is this just data timing?
I saw that too. My guess is the HQLA haircuts refreshed overnight. I'll pull the RiskEngine exposure snapshot and compare against what ReportingBI is reading.
Thanks. Also worth checking whether the 30-day outflow assumptions for the committed credit lines got updated. That alone could move it a few points.
Joining late. I need a firm LCR figure before the 4pm treasury sync. Which number should I be quoting, 128 or 134?
Don't quote either yet, Martin. We're reconciling the two now and I'd rather give you one number we can defend. Should have an answer within the hour.
Fine, but flag me the moment you know. If it's really 128 I want to talk through the buffer before the sync.

Found part of it. RiskEngine intraday position snapshot picked up about $62M of additional Level 2A securities that weren't in the prior pack, so that's a point in the numerator. Not the whole gap though.
Okay, that's the opposite direction, it should push LCR up. So the denominator must have gone up more. Checking outflow tabs now.

Update: the denominator shift is from the undrawn facility run-off rate. Someone changed the corporate revolver bucket from 10% to 15% in the ReportingBI config on Tuesday. Looks like it was a deliberate change with a ticket attached.
That was me, actually. Treasury asked for a more conservative run-off assumption after the audit comments. I should have told you both. Does that fully explain 128?
Mostly. With the 15% run-off plus the extra Level 2A securities, I get 129.4% on my side. Remaining 1.4 points looks like a rounding and cutoff time mismatch in the dashboard.
Agreed. The dashboard is pulling positions at 11:30 while my RiskEngine run is at 12:45. I'll rerun the dashboard refresh and confirm they line up.
Refreshed ReportingBI after the 12:45 snapshot landed. Dashboard now reads 129.3%, within a tenth of our manual calc. We're good.
Great, I'll use 129% for the 4pm sync and note the run-off change as the driver versus yesterday's 134%. Thanks both, and I'll loop you in on config changes going forward.
